subject: Multi-cloud marketplace offering priority & bundling strategy
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-cloud marketplace SKU & regional priority proposal

Team —

Summary: we need a tight, pragmatic decision on which marketplace SKUs and bundles we prioritize for the next 90-day co-sell push (AWS first, then GCP, then Azure). The product/partner asks are coming fast; marketing needs SKU names and short descriptions by EoW.

Key constraints:
- Limited engineering bandwidth for separate marketplace images; favor a small set of canonical SKUs that map cleanly to our dedicated/dedicated-light/private offers.
- Sales wants 2 packaged bundles (Standard / Enterprise) per cloud for co-sell enablement.
- Pricing should align with existing usage tiers and not create duplicate SKUs across clouds.

Proposal (attached: redwood_marketplace_offering_matrix_v2.xlsx):
1) AWS (priority #1):
   - SKU A: redwood-core-standard — 8 vCPU / 32GB RAM equivalent, single-model reference (cost-conscious).
   - SKU B: redwood-core-enterprise — 16 vCPU / 64GB RAM equivalent, includes KV cache + longer context.
   - Region set: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), EU (Ireland) for initial launch.
2) GCP (priority #2):
   - SKU names mirror AWS but append "-gcp" for internal tracking (we avoid public duplication).
   - Regions: us-central1, europe-west1.
3) Azure (priority #3):
   - Start with a single Standard SKU for co-sell pilots; add Enterprise after first quarter.

Open questions for this thread:
- Does infra/ops (Jonas/Karthik) see any blocker to packing those two SKUs across the three clouds without splitting into many images?
- Marissa: what co-sell collateral do you need from GTM/marketing to support AWS GTM by June 8?
- Any compliance/regulatory regional restrictions we should avoid?

Please reply inline with red/yellow/green for each bullet. If green, assume we push to the marketplace listing draft and schedule a joint listing call with each cloud partner.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Partner GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_marketplace_offering_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace SKU & regional priority proposal

Priya —

Quick status and notes (inline):

1) AWS SKUs: GREEN
   - We can maintain a single AMI/container image per SKU family with cloud-specific packaging layers. That avoids duplicate engineering work.
   - Suggest we define a single reference image and then a thin packaging job to generate AWS/GCP/Azure artifacts.

2) GCP naming: YELLOW
   - Mirroring names is fine internally, but external listing names should be localized per cloud UX. We should ask marketplace PMs how strict they are about display names.

3) Regions: GREEN for US/EU baseline; RED flag for aggressive regional expansion immediately. We should conserve images and add regions after initial metrics.

Other technical asks:
- We need a canonical set of feature-flag mappings (which SKU exposes KV cache, which includes model quantization). Add that column to the matrix.
- For Enterprise SKU we should bake in telemetry opt-in documentation for cloud marketplaces (compliance asks).

Attaching a small ops workplan snippet to run packaging jobs and estimated time: 3 engineer-weeks to automate the thin-packaging pipeline (can parallelize).

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace SKU & regional priority proposal

Hi Priya / team —

Thanks for the clear proposal — AWS Marketplace is enthusiastic about a focused SKU set. A few items from our side: 

1) Co-sell readiness: we prefer two SKUs (Standard + Enterprise) for co-sell qualification. GREEN.
2) Listing names: AWS listing UX requires a short public name and an internal SKU code; please provide both.
3) Pricing alignment: we will need suggested list price bands for Standard and Enterprise and any volume-discount thresholds.
4) AWS-specific requirement: marketplace security questionnaire (minimal) and an IAM role mapping doc.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync next week with the AWS listing team, product infra, and GTM? Our listing lead (Sarah) can invite the paperwork team if you confirm pricing bands.

Two immediate asks from me:
- Please upload the updated matrix to the Drive link and add a column for "public listing name" and "internal code".
- Attach a sample pricing band (e.g., $0.10/token for Standard; $0.06/token enterprise committed).

We can fast-track co-sell enablement once the AWS listing is live in the US East / US West regions.

Best,
Sarah Chen
Sr. Partner Development Manager — AWS Marketplace
Amazon Web Services

Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace SKU & regional priority proposal

Thanks everyone — quick summary and decisions from Redwood to move forward: 

Decisions (actionable):
- Approve initial SKU set: redwood-core-standard, redwood-core-enterprise (internal codes: RDI-S, RDI-E).
- Regions for launch: us-east-1 (N. Virginia), us-west-2 (Oregon), europe-west1 (Ireland).
- GCP listing will mirror AWS feature set but use display names tailored to GCP UX.
- Azure will be pilot-only with Standard SKU in Q3, add Enterprise after performance review.

Actions (owners / ETA):
- Marissa: finalize co-sell marketing one-pager and AWS-ready collateral by 2026-06-08. (owner: marissa_cole)
- Jonas & Karthik: deliver thin-packaging pipeline + feature-flag matrix update by 2026-06-01. (owners: jonas_weber, karthik_iyer)
- Priya: schedule AWS listing sync and share pricing bands to Sarah by 2026-05-28. (owner: priya_natarajan)
- All: update Drive matrix (link above) with "public listing name", "internal code", and pricing bands.

Attachments: co-sell_playbook_draft_v1.pdf (pdf) — this is a rough GTM play for the first 90 days; feedback welcome.

If there are no objections by EoD Thursday (2026-05-27) we will treat these as committed and begin listing prep.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Natarajan
